title: Policy sandbox: deterministic dry-run simulator for per-tenant batching/cache effects
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Summary: Build a deterministic 'policy sandbox' that can dry-run proposed per-customer and per-route batching/cache configuration changes against historical traces and short synthetic replays. The sandbox outputs a ranked recommendation set (batch size, KV prefetch window, cache TTL, allowlist/denylist flags, tier mapping) with cost delta, latency P95 delta, and a confidence score.

Goals:
- Give SRE/Platform teams a low-risk way to validate cost-saving changes before live apply.
- Support per-customer and per-route segmentation: simulate changes only for targeted customer IDs or route patterns and respect tier controls.
- Produce safe rollout actions: canary apply plan, automatic rollback triggers, and human-readable runbook.

Approach:
- Replay engine: deterministic replay from sampled request traces (KV cache hits, sequence lengths, prompt prefixes) plus a lightweight synthetic generator for corner cases.
- Cost model: token-level cost estimator + GPU throughput model that factors batching efficiency curves and KV cache hit-rate sensitivity.
- Policy synthesis: propose small-step changes (eg. batch +2, TTL -50ms) and score each via Bayesian bootstrap to estimate confidence under variance.
- Safety layer: apply only to routes/customers not on a denylist; respect allowlists and tier-based minimums (gold customers get stricter latency guards).
- Apply/rollback plan: generate a stepwise canary (1%, 10%, 50%) with automated metric checks (latency P95, error rate, tokens/sec, business metric if available).

Trade-offs & risks:
- Replay fidelity vs runtime cost: full fidelity traces are expensive; we will start with representative sampled windows and fall back to synthetic augmentation.
- Model mismatch: simulator is an approximation. Mitigation: conservative confidence thresholds and short canary windows.
- Complexity of per-customer rules: start with tier+route combos and iterate for custom policies.

Acceptance criteria:
- Sandbox can ingest a trace file and produce recommendations for a route and a customer segment within 30 minutes.
- Recommendations include at least batch size, cache TTL, and allowlist/denylist decision with cost and latency projections.
- Confidence scoring implemented; recommendations tagged low/medium/high.
- End-to-end canary apply workflow exists: create canary, monitor metrics, auto-rollback on threshold breach.
- Documentation and runbook for SRE and Solutions engineers.

Metrics to track:
- Estimated tokens-cost delta (USD) and actual post-apply delta.
- Latency P95 change forecast vs observed.
- False-positive rate of safe-rollback triggers.

Rollout plan:
1) Prototype replay harness + cost model (spike) -> internal demo (owner: Liam Chen)
2) Integrate tier/allowlist logic and confidence scoring -> internal evals on historical production windows
3) Implement canary apply + rollback automation in console + API hooks
4) Beta with two pilot customers (low-risk routes)
5) Wide release with runbook and training

Open questions:
- How to represent complex customer-tier overrides in policy DSL? (short-term: key-value mapping table)
- What confidence threshold maps to 1% vs 10% canary? (to be tuned during pilot)

Notes: prototype cost model lives in docs link; PR will be created under infra/sandbox-replay.

comments: 2026-03-06 - Spike complete: replay harness prototype can replay sampled traces with cache-hit annotations. Prototype identified a 12% cost saving on a 5% subset when batch +3 and TTL -100ms were applied in simulation.
2026-03-09 - Design review with PM (Carlos Mendes): agreed to prioritize conservative defaults for Gold customers and require explicit allowlist exemptions for aggressive optimizations.
2026-03-10 - Engineering review: moved to Bayesian bootstrap for confidence to better capture variance in small-sample replays. Liam to own integration with telemetry ingestion.
2026-03-12 - Added allowlist/denylist data model and discriminator for per-route policy inheritance. Decided to gate arbitrary policy edits behind platform-role to avoid accidental mass-rollouts.

2026-03-14 - QA smoke run started on internal canary pipeline; initial runs passed functional checks but showed higher-than-expected P95 variance for long-tail routes. Next: tune synthetic generator and widen trace sampling.
